text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The cabinet has decided to raise the price of natural gas by 18.8 percent, electricity by 24.9 percent and that of district heating by 21.9 percent from January 1, 1997. @

- The cabinet decided yesterday to raise pensions by 19.5 percent on average next year. The cabinet also decided to reduce expenditures in next year's budget by HUF 14-14.5 billion. The National Bank informed the cabinet that foreign currency reserves allow the Bank to repay $1 billion in external state debt ahead of schedule.
- Observers predict an extremely sharp debate at this weekend's Free Democrat party congress on the state of the coalition and the state of the party. @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn has proposed journalist Jozsef Meruk, the Socialist Party's campaign chief in 1990, for the post of director general of the Hungarian News Agency MTI.

- The economic situation in Hungary is marked by stagnation and decline, according to the Privatisation Research Institute's prognosis for 1997. An economic policy focused on growth and human resources, would improve matters, said company director Gyorgy Matolcsy.
- A 39-year-old entrepreneur is in critical condition after an unidentified person pumped four bullets into his body outside his house in Budapest Wednesday night. @
- Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky yesterday offered HUF 250 million in support to Budapest police to help restore law and order in the capital.

- Young Democrat vice president Zoltan Illes, an expert on environmental protection, said chemical agents identical in origin and composition to the hazardous waste stored at the Letenye border station, is being stored in Budapest 21st and 3rd districts.
NAPI GAZDASAG @
- The central budget deficit was HUF 75.5 billion for the first ten months of 1996, excluding the HUF 65 billion deficit of the social security system.
- The equity of Unicbank Rt. is likely to be increased by HUF 2.64 billion to HUF 7 billion at the bank's general meeting on December 16.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Ethics Committee of the Association of the Hungarian Banks has reprimanded Citibank for misleading clients in an ad. @
- The general meeting of the Hungarian Investment and Development Bank will probably establish the Hungarian Development Bank, the legal successor of the present establishment, on December 23.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Young Democrat Viktor Orban, chairman of Parliament's integration committee, Thursday called on European Parliament deputies to settle several issues harmful to Hungary.
- The traditional sausage manufacturer Pick Rt. is likely to reach annual revenue of HUF 26 billion this year.
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- Those interested in Central European stock markets should invest in Hungarian and Polish shares, the London-based investment bank HSBC James Capel advises.
